title: Ravina bar Shila
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: He is mentioned only in halakhah, and Rav Chisda received from him, as we find “Rav Chisda said that Ravina bar Shila said” in Sukkah 13a, twice, Moed Katan 17b and Yevamot 68b. In Zevachim 36a it reads bar Sila, and Hyman proposes bar Shila, as the statement is cited in the Kesef Mishneh, Hilkhot Pesulei HaMukdashin 14:9.
In Pesachim 59a it reads “Ravina said that Rav Chisda said,” and Hyman proposes the reverse: “Rav Chisda said that Ravina bar Shila said,” as cited in Dikdukei Soferim.
In Zevachim 89b: “Ravina bar Shila said: The sacrificial portions of holy offerings,” etc.
In Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 2:3: “Rabbi Zeira said: Binah bar Shila recited [a baraita].”

notes.text: ב״פ is read as twice and כ״מ as Kesef Mishneh. Hyman’s only-in-halakhah assertion and proposed Shila/Sila and transmission reversals remain attributed. תני in the Jerusalem Talmud notice is the baraita-reciter role.

Two separate consulted Sukkah 13a passages have Rav Chisda reporting Ravina bar Shila. This does not by itself establish the universal “only in halakhah” assertion, or verify the Kesef Mishneh and Dikdukei Soferim readings reported by Hyman.
